markdown:
# Massachusetts Commercial Solar Incentives

Our current research does not list Massachusetts commercial solar incentives, so we cannot name programs or values without guessing. Below is what our data does cover and what we would need to answer the question properly.

## What our data covers

- **Live solar-related work.** The opportunity radar tracks 25 Massachusetts items. One is the Massport Worcester Regional Airport 149A trade-contractor RFQ. Its scope includes renewable energy upgrades alongside electrical, fire alarm and lighting. It is due Oct 8, 2026, which is today (CET opportunity radar).
- **Gaps in state sources.** Automated pulls from mass.gov and COMMBUYS were blocked. That means state program pages were not captured (CET opportunity radar).
- **Solar in the growth plan.** Phase 3 names solar and storage O&M as one of the service lines that turn one-off bids into recurring contracts (CET growth plan).
- **Recurring mix target.** The month-36 roadmap assumes about 25% recurring service mix. This is a labelled assumption, not guidance (CET growth plan).

## Data that would answer it

| Question | Data needed |
|---|---|
| Which state incentives apply to commercial projects | Current state energy agency program rules and remaining capacity |
| Federal tax credit status for 2026 starts | Current Treasury guidance, reviewed by the customer's tax adviser |
| Net metering and interconnection terms | Massachusetts distribution utility tariffs and queue data |
| Incentive value to a typical customer | Our own past solar bids and customer financial models |

Eligibility and tax treatment are questions for each customer's own advisers. We do not give legal, tax or compliance advice.

## How we can help today

- We scope and install commercial electrical and renewable energy upgrades from Worcester and Taunton.
- We can price a project once the customer confirms which incentives they are pursuing.

Incentive terms decide whether customers build solar at all. Each install we win is also a feed for the O&M contracts the growth plan relies on to raise recurring revenue (est.).

## Next actions

1. Confirm the Worcester Regional Airport 149A RFQ submission went in today, Oct 8, 2026. Tag its renewable scope in the radar.
2. Pull current Massachusetts solar incentive rules and utility tariffs by hand, since automated access was blocked. Store them as a dated reference sheet.
3. Pull our past solar bids to estimate typical project size and incentive dependence. Label all results est.
4. Draft a solar and storage O&M offer to attach to every solar install bid, in line with Phase 3.
